# French Grammar Tables
One place for the small words and patterns you need every day: articles, pronouns, possessives, this and that, question words, negatives, adjectives, prepositions, a verb summary, and numbers, dates and the time. Each table says when to use it, gives every French item with its pronunciation and a Listen button, then examples and the mistakes to watch out for. Pronunciations use the same English-style respelling as the verb guides (no IPA). Tables marked Preview go a little beyond A2.
## Pronunciation key
| Spelling | Sounds like |
|---|---|
| **zh** | the "s" in *measure* (French **j** / soft **g**) |
| **uh** | the "a" in *about* |
| **ew** | French **u**: say "ee" with your lips rounded like "oo" |
| **N** (capital) | nasal vowel: hum the vowel through your nose, don't say the "n" |
| **ahN** | nasal *an / en* (as in *France*) |
| **ohN** | nasal *on* (as in *bon*) |
| **aN** | nasal *in / ain / ien* (as in *vin*) |
| **uhN** | nasal *un* (as in *un*) |
| **r** | French throaty "r", made at the back of the throat |
| **‿** | liaison: the silent final consonant is pronounced at the start of the next word (*vous‿avez* = voo zah-vay) |

Tips: final consonants are usually silent (*parlent* = "parl"). A hyphen joins syllables said as one word; a liaison consonant is written at the start of the next syllable (*les amis* = lay zah-mee).

## 1. Articles
Almost every French noun comes with a small word in front of it. These tables show which one to use.
### Definite articles: the
*When:* For a specific thing ("the book"), and for things in general after verbs of liking: J'aime le café = I like coffee.
| French | Pronunciation | English | Gender / number |
|---|---|---|---|
| le | luh | the | m. sing. |
| la | lah | the | f. sing. |
| l' | l | the | sing., before a vowel or mute h |
| les | lay | the | pl. (m. and f.) |
- **Le train arrive.** (luh traN ah-reev) — *The train is arriving.*
- **La gare est loin.** (lah gar eh lwaN) — *The station is far.*
- **L'hôtel est petit.** (loh-tel eh puh-tee) — *The hotel is small.*
- **J'aime les chats.** (zhem lay shah) — *I like cats.*
> **Watch out**
> - ✗ *J'aime café.* → ✓ **J'aime le café.** (zhem luh kah-fay) — French keeps the article for things in general.
> - ✗ *le ami* → ✓ **l'ami** (lah-mee) — le and la become l' before a vowel or a mute h.
> - les before a vowel makes a liaison z: les amis (lay zah-mee).
### Indefinite articles: a, an, some
*When:* For one thing that isn't specific ("a book"), and des for "some" with things you can count.
| French | Pronunciation | English | Gender / number |
|---|---|---|---|
| un | uhN | a, an | m. sing. |
| une | ewn | a, an | f. sing. |
| des | day | some | pl. (m. and f.) |
- **J'ai un frère.** (zhay uhN frair) — *I have a brother.*
- **Elle a une voiture.** (el ah ewn vwah-tewr) — *She has a car.*
- **Il y a des pommes.** (eel ee ah day pum) — *There are (some) apples.*
- **Je suis professeur.** (zhuh swee proh-feh-suhr) — *I am a teacher. (no article for a job after être)*
> **Watch out**
> - ✗ *Je suis un professeur.* → ✓ **Je suis professeur.** (zhuh swee proh-feh-suhr) — no un/une before a job after être.
> - ✗ *J'ai pommes.* → ✓ **J'ai des pommes.** (zhay day pum) — English can drop "some"; French can't drop des.
### Partitive articles: some
*When:* For an amount of something you can't count: some bread, some water. Very common with food and drink, after manger, boire, prendre and vouloir.
| French | Pronunciation | English | Gender / number |
|---|---|---|---|
| du | dew | some | m. |
| de la | duh lah | some | f. |
| de l' | duh l | some | before a vowel or mute h |
| des | day | some | pl. |
- **Je voudrais du pain.** (zhuh voo-dreh dew paN) — *I'd like some bread.*
- **Tu bois de la bière ?** (tew bwah duh lah byair) — *Do you drink beer?*
- **Il prend de l'eau.** (eel prahN duh loh) — *He's having some water.*
- **Nous mangeons des légumes.** (noo mahN-zhohN day lay-gewm) — *We eat vegetables.*
> **Watch out**
> - ✗ *Je mange pain.* → ✓ **Je mange du pain.** (zhuh mahNzh dew paN) — an amount of something always takes du / de la / de l'.
> - ✗ *J'aime du café.* → ✓ **J'aime le café.** (zhem luh kah-fay) — after aimer, adorer, détester and préférer use le/la/les (things in general).

See also: manger · boire · prendre.
### À and de + the article: au, aux, du, des
*When:* à (to, at) and de (of, from) melt together with le and les. They do not change with la or l'.
| French | Pronunciation | English | Made from |
|---|---|---|---|
| au | oh | to the, at the | à + le |
| à la | ah lah | to the, at the | à + la (no change) |
| à l' | ah l | to the, at the | à + l' (no change) |
| aux | oh | to the, at the | à + les |
| du | dew | of the, from the | de + le |
| de la | duh lah | of the, from the | de + la (no change) |
| de l' | duh l | of the, from the | de + l' (no change) |
| des | day | of the, from the | de + les |
- **Je vais au cinéma.** (zhuh veh oh see-nay-mah) — *I'm going to the cinema.*
- **Elle est à la gare.** (el eh tah lah gar) — *She is at the station.*
- **Il parle aux enfants.** (eel parl oh zahN-fahN) — *He is talking to the children.*
- **Je reviens du marché.** (zhuh ruh-vyaN dew mar-shay) — *I'm coming back from the market.*
> **Watch out**
> - ✗ *Je vais à le parc.* → ✓ **Je vais au parc.** (zhuh veh oh park) — à + le is always au.
> - ✗ *la porte de le garage* → ✓ **la porte du garage** (lah port dew gah-rahzh) — de + le is always du.
### Pas de: after a negative
*When:* After a negative, un, une, du, de la, de l' and des all become de (d' before a vowel). Exception: after être, keep the article.
| French | Pronunciation | English | Use |
|---|---|---|---|
| pas de | pah duh | no, not any | before a consonant |
| pas d' | pah d | no, not any | before a vowel or mute h |
| plus de | plew duh | no more | ne ... plus |
| jamais de | zhah-meh duh | never any | ne ... jamais |
- **Je n'ai pas de voiture.** (zhuh nay pah duh vwah-tewr) — *I don't have a car.*
- **Il ne boit pas d'alcool.** (eel nuh bwah pah dahl-kohl) — *He doesn't drink alcohol.*
- **Nous n'avons plus de pain.** (noo nah-vohN plew duh paN) — *We have no more bread.*
- **Ce n'est pas un problème.** (suh neh pah zuhN proh-blem) — *It isn't a problem. (after être, keep un)*
> **Watch out**
> - ✗ *Je n'ai pas une voiture.* → ✓ **Je n'ai pas de voiture.** (zhuh nay pah duh vwah-tewr) — un/une/des become de after pas.
> - ✗ *Je n'aime pas de café.* → ✓ **Je n'aime pas le café.** (zhuh nem pah luh kah-fay) — le/la/les don't change.

See also: Negative words.
### Which article?
*When:* A quick decision guide: what you mean decides the article.
| French | Pronunciation | English | Example |
|---|---|---|---|
| le, la, les | luh, lah, lay | the, things in general | J'aime le thé. |
| un, une | uhN, ewn | one countable thing | Je veux une pomme. |
| des | day | several countable things | Je veux des pommes. |
| du, de la | dew, duh lah | an amount you can't count | Je veux du thé. |
| de | duh | after a negative | Je ne veux pas de thé. |
- **Je prends un café et de l'eau.** (zhuh prahN uhN kah-fay ay duh loh) — *I'll have a coffee and some water.*
- **Le café est chaud.** (luh kah-fay eh shoh) — *The coffee is hot.*
> **Watch out**
> - In English you can often say nothing ("I eat bread"); in French a noun almost always needs an article.
## 2. Pronouns
### Subject pronouns
*When:* Who does the action. They come before the verb.
| French | Pronunciation | English | Use |
|---|---|---|---|
| je | zhuh | I | j' before a vowel |
| tu | tew | you | one person, informal |
| il | eel | he, it | m. |
| elle | el | she, it | f. |
| on | ohN | we, one, people | il/elle verb form |
| nous | noo | we |  |
| vous | voo | you | formal, or more than one person |
| ils | eel | they | m. or mixed group |
| elles | el | they | f. only |
- **On va au cinéma ?** (ohN vah oh see-nay-mah) — *Shall we go to the cinema?*
- **Vous êtes prêts ?** (voo zet preh) — *Are you (all) ready?*
- **Ils arrivent demain.** (eel zah-reev duh-maN) — *They arrive tomorrow.*
> **Watch out**
> - ✗ *On allons au parc.* → ✓ **On va au parc.** (ohN vah oh park) — on means "we" but takes the il/elle form.
> - A group of nine women and one man is ils, not elles.
### Stressed pronouns: moi, toi...
*When:* On their own (Moi !), after a preposition (avec moi, chez toi), after c'est, and for emphasis (Moi, je reste.).
| French | Pronunciation | English | Gender / number |
|---|---|---|---|
| moi | mwah | me |  |
| toi | twah | you |  |
| lui | lwee | him | m. |
| elle | el | her | f. |
| nous | noo | us |  |
| vous | voo | you |  |
| eux | uh | them | m. or mixed |
| elles | el | them | f. |
- **Tu viens avec moi ?** (tew vyaN ah-vek mwah) — *Are you coming with me?*
- **C'est pour lui.** (seh poor lwee) — *It's for him.*
- **Moi, je préfère le thé.** (mwah, zhuh pray-fair luh tay) — *Me, I prefer tea.*
- **On mange chez eux.** (ohN mahNzh shay zuh) — *We're eating at their place.*
> **Watch out**
> - ✗ *avec je* → ✓ **avec moi** (ah-vek mwah) — after a preposition use the stressed form.
> - ✗ *Je aussi.* → ✓ **Moi aussi.** (mwah oh-see) — on its own, use moi.
### Direct object pronouns: me, le, la...
*When:* They replace the thing or person that receives the action directly (no à): Je vois Marie → Je la vois. They go before the verb.
| French | Pronunciation | English | Use |
|---|---|---|---|
| me | muh | me | m' before a vowel |
| te | tuh | you | t' before a vowel |
| le | luh | him, it | m.; l' before a vowel |
| la | lah | her, it | f.; l' before a vowel |
| nous | noo | us |  |
| vous | voo | you |  |
| les | lay | them | pl. |
- **Je le vois.** (zhuh luh vwah) — *I see him / it.*
- **Tu la connais ?** (tew lah koh-neh) — *Do you know her?*
- **Il m'aime.** (eel mem) — *He loves me.*
- **Je les achète.** (zhuh lay zah-shet) — *I'm buying them.*
> **Watch out**
> - ✗ *Je vois le.* → ✓ **Je le vois.** (zhuh luh vwah) — the pronoun goes before the verb.
> - ✗ *Je regarde lui.* → ✓ **Je le regarde.** (zhuh luh ruh-gard) — regarder takes a direct object: le, not lui.

See also: Order of object pronouns.
### Indirect object pronouns: me, lui, leur...
*When:* They replace à + a person: Je parle à Paul → Je lui parle. Common with parler à, donner à, dire à, téléphoner à, écrire à and demander à.
| French | Pronunciation | English | Use |
|---|---|---|---|
| me | muh | to me | m' before a vowel |
| te | tuh | to you | t' before a vowel |
| lui | lwee | to him, to her | m. and f. |
| nous | noo | to us |  |
| vous | voo | to you |  |
| leur | luhr | to them | m. and f.; never leurs |
- **Je lui parle.** (zhuh lwee parl) — *I'm talking to him / to her.*
- **Tu leur téléphones ?** (tew luhr tay-lay-fohn) — *Are you phoning them?*
- **Elle m'écrit.** (el may-kree) — *She writes to me.*
> **Watch out**
> - ✗ *Je leurs donne.* → ✓ **Je leur donne.** (zhuh luhr dun) — the pronoun leur never takes an s.
> - ✗ *Je la téléphone.* → ✓ **Je lui téléphone.** (zhuh lwee tay-lay-fohn) — téléphoner à: indirect.

See also: parler · donner · dire.
### Reflexive pronouns
*When:* With pronominal verbs (se lever, s'appeler) the action comes back to the subject. The full lessons are in the Reflexive verbs topic.
| French | Pronunciation | English | With |
|---|---|---|---|
| me | muh | myself | je; m' before a vowel |
| te | tuh | yourself | tu; t' before a vowel |
| se | suh | himself, herself, itself | il, elle, on; s' before a vowel |
| nous | noo | ourselves | nous |
| vous | voo | yourself, yourselves | vous |
| se | suh | themselves | ils, elles; s' before a vowel |
- **Je me lève à sept heures.** (zhuh muh lev ah set uhr) — *I get up at seven.*
- **Comment tu t'appelles ?** (koh-mahN tew tah-pel) — *What's your name?*
- **Nous nous habillons.** (noo noo zah-bee-yohN) — *We're getting dressed.*
> **Watch out**
> - ✗ *Je lève à sept heures.* → ✓ **Je me lève à sept heures.** (zhuh muh lev ah set uhr) — keep the pronoun even when English has no "myself".

See also: Reflexive verbs, lesson 1 · se lever · s'appeler.
### Y and en
*When:* y replaces à + a place or thing (there, about it); en replaces de + a thing, and any quantity (some, of it, of them).
| French | Pronunciation | English | Use |
|---|---|---|---|
| y | ee | there, about it | replaces à + place / thing |
| en | ahN | some, any, of it, of them, from there | replaces de + thing, or a quantity |
| il y a | eel ee ah | there is, there are | fixed phrase |
| j'en ai deux | zhahN nay duh | I have two (of them) | en + number |
- **Tu vas à Paris ? Oui, j'y vais.** (tew vah zah pah-ree / wee, zhee veh) — *Are you going to Paris? Yes, I'm going (there).*
- **Je pense à mon travail. J'y pense.** (zhuh pahNs ah mohN trah-vahy / zhee pahNs) — *I'm thinking about my work. I'm thinking about it.*
- **Tu veux du café ? Oui, j'en veux.** (tew vuh dew kah-fay / wee, zhahN vuh) — *Do you want some coffee? Yes, I want some.*
- **Combien de frères as-tu ? J'en ai deux.** (kohN-byaN duh frair ah-tew / zhahN nay duh) — *How many brothers do you have? I have two.*
> **Watch out**
> - ✗ *Oui, je vais.* → ✓ **Oui, j'y vais.** (wee, zhee veh) — aller needs a place: use y.
> - ✗ *J'ai deux.* → ✓ **J'en ai deux.** (zhahN nay duh) — with a number and no noun, add en.
> - For people, use lui/leur or à + a stressed pronoun, not y: Je pense à elle (zhuh pahNs ah el).
### Order of object pronouns (Preview)
*When:* When two object pronouns go before the verb, they follow this order (B1).
| French | Pronunciation | English | Position |
|---|---|---|---|
| me, te, se, nous, vous | muh, tuh, suh, noo, voo | me, you, oneself, us, you | 1st |
| le, la, les | luh, lah, lay | him, her, it, them | 2nd |
| lui, leur | lwee, luhr | to him / her, to them | 3rd |
| y | ee | there | 4th |
| en | ahN | some, of it | 5th |
- **Il me le donne.** (eel muh luh dun) — *He gives it to me.*
- **Je le lui donne.** (zhuh luh lwee dun) — *I give it to him / her.*
- **Je vous en prie.** (zhuh voo zahN pree) — *You're welcome. (set phrase)*
- **Il y en a trois.** (eel ee ahN nah trwah) — *There are three (of them).*
> **Watch out**
> - ✗ *Je lui le donne.* → ✓ **Je le lui donne.** (zhuh luh lwee dun) — le/la/les come before lui/leur.
> - In a compound tense the pronouns go before avoir/être: Je le lui ai donné (zhuh luh lwee ay doh-nay).
### Relative pronouns: qui, que, où, dont
*When:* They join two sentences about the same noun ("the man who...", "the film that...").
| French | Pronunciation | English | Replaces |
|---|---|---|---|
| qui | kee | who, which, that | the subject (a verb follows) |
| que | kuh | whom, which, that | the object (a subject follows); qu' before a vowel |
| où | oo | where, when | a place or a time |
| dont | dohN | whose, of which, about which | de + noun (B1) |
- **L'homme qui parle est mon père.** (lum kee parl eh mohN pair) — *The man who is talking is my father.*
- **Le film que je regarde est long.** (luh feelm kuh zhuh ruh-gard eh lohN) — *The film (that) I'm watching is long.*
- **La ville où j'habite est petite.** (lah veel oo zhah-beet eh puh-teet) — *The town where I live is small.*
- **Le livre dont je parle est ici.** (luh leevr dohN zhuh parl eh tee-see) — *The book I'm talking about is here.*
> **Watch out**
> - ✗ *le film qui je regarde* → ✓ **le film que je regarde** (luh feelm kuh zhuh ruh-gard) — a subject (je) follows, so que.
> - English often drops "that"; French never drops que.
## 3. Possessives
### Possessive adjectives: my, your, his...
*When:* Before a noun. They agree with the THING owned, not the owner: sa voiture = his car or her car.
| French | Pronunciation | English | With |
|---|---|---|---|
| mon | mohN | my | m. sing.; f. before a vowel |
| ma | mah | my | f. sing. |
| mes | may | my | pl. |
| ton | tohN | your | m. sing.; f. before a vowel |
| ta | tah | your | f. sing. |
| tes | tay | your | pl. |
| son | sohN | his, her, its | m. sing.; f. before a vowel |
| sa | sah | his, her, its | f. sing. |
| ses | say | his, her, its | pl. |
| notre | noh-truh | our | sing. |
| nos | noh | our | pl. |
| votre | voh-truh | your | sing. |
| vos | voh | your | pl. |
| leur | luhr | their | sing. |
| leurs | luhr | their | pl. |
- **C'est mon amie Claire.** (seh mohN nah-mee klair) — *This is my friend Claire. (amie is f., but mon before a vowel)*
- **Paul aime sa mère.** (pohl em sah mair) — *Paul loves his mother.*
- **Marie aime son père.** (mah-ree em sohN pair) — *Marie loves her father.*
- **Ils vendent leur maison.** (eel vahNd luhr meh-zohN) — *They're selling their house.*
> **Watch out**
> - ✗ *ma amie* → ✓ **mon amie** (mohN nah-mee) — ma, ta, sa become mon, ton, son before a vowel.
> - ✗ *Marie aime sa père.* → ✓ **Marie aime son père.** (mah-ree em sohN pair) — agree with père (m.), not with Marie.
### Possessive pronouns: mine, yours...
*When:* They replace possessive + noun: mon livre → le mien (mine). They agree with the thing owned.
| French | Pronunciation | English | Gender / number |
|---|---|---|---|
| le mien | luh myaN | mine | m. sing. |
| la mienne | lah myen | mine | f. sing. |
| les miens | lay myaN | mine | m. pl. |
| les miennes | lay myen | mine | f. pl. |
| le tien | luh tyaN | yours | m. sing. |
| la tienne | lah tyen | yours | f. sing. |
| les tiens | lay tyaN | yours | m. pl. |
| les tiennes | lay tyen | yours | f. pl. |
| le sien | luh syaN | his, hers | m. sing. |
| la sienne | lah syen | his, hers | f. sing. |
| les siens | lay syaN | his, hers | m. pl. |
| les siennes | lay syen | his, hers | f. pl. |
| le nôtre | luh noh-truh | ours | m. sing. |
| la nôtre | lah noh-truh | ours | f. sing. |
| les nôtres | lay noh-truh | ours | pl. |
| le vôtre | luh voh-truh | yours | m. sing. |
| la vôtre | lah voh-truh | yours | f. sing. |
| les vôtres | lay voh-truh | yours | pl. |
| le leur | luh luhr | theirs | m. sing. |
| la leur | lah luhr | theirs | f. sing. |
| les leurs | lay luhr | theirs | pl. |
- **Ce n'est pas ton stylo, c'est le mien.** (suh neh pah tohN stee-loh, seh luh myaN) — *It's not your pen, it's mine.*
- **Ta voiture est rouge, la mienne est bleue.** (tah vwah-tewr eh roozh, lah myen eh bluh) — *Your car is red; mine is blue.*
- **Nos enfants jouent avec les leurs.** (noh zahN-fahN zhoo ah-vek lay luhr) — *Our children play with theirs.*
> **Watch out**
> - ✗ *C'est mien.* → ✓ **C'est le mien.** (seh luh myaN) — keep the article. Casual alternative: C'est à moi (seh tah mwah).
> - notre and votre (no accent) vs le nôtre and le vôtre (with an accent, a longer o). Both are respelled noh / voh.
## 4. Demonstratives
### Demonstrative adjectives: this, that, these
*When:* Before a noun to point at it: this / that / these / those. Add -ci (here) or -là (there) to contrast.
| French | Pronunciation | English | With |
|---|---|---|---|
| ce | suh | this, that | m. sing. |
| cet | set | this, that | m. sing. before a vowel or mute h |
| cette | set | this, that | f. sing. |
| ces | say | these, those | pl. |
| ce livre-ci | suh leevr-see | this book (here) | -ci = here |
| ce livre-là | suh leevr-lah | that book (there) | -là = there |
- **Ce café est délicieux.** (suh kah-fay eh day-lee-syuh) — *This coffee is delicious.*
- **Cet hôtel est cher.** (set oh-tel eh shair) — *This hotel is expensive.*
- **Cette semaine, je travaille.** (set suh-men, zhuh trah-vahy) — *This week I'm working.*
- **Tu préfères cette robe-ci ou cette robe-là ?** (tew pray-fair set rob-see oo set rob-lah) — *Do you prefer this dress or that one?*
> **Watch out**
> - ✗ *ce homme* → ✓ **cet homme** (set um) — before a vowel or mute h, the masculine is cet.
> - ✗ *cet femme* → ✓ **cette femme** (set fahm) — cet and cette sound the same, but cet is only masculine.
> - Liaison: ces amis (say zah-mee).
### Demonstrative pronouns: this one, that one (Preview)
*When:* They replace ce/cette/ces + noun. Never alone: always followed by -ci / -là, qui / que, or de (B1).
| French | Pronunciation | English | Gender / number |
|---|---|---|---|
| celui | suh-lwee | the one, this one | m. sing. |
| celle | sel | the one, this one | f. sing. |
| ceux | suh | the ones, these | m. pl. |
| celles | sel | the ones, these | f. pl. |
| celui-ci | suh-lwee-see | this one (here) | m. sing. |
| celle-là | sel-lah | that one (there) | f. sing. |
- **Je prends celui-ci.** (zhuh prahN suh-lwee-see) — *I'll take this one. (un pull)*
- **C'est celle de ma sœur.** (seh sel duh mah suhr) — *It's my sister's. (la voiture)*
- **Ceux qui veulent venir sont les bienvenus.** (suh kee vuhl vuh-neer sohN lay byaN-vuh-new) — *Those who want to come are welcome.*
- **Quelle robe ? Celle que tu portes.** (kel rob / sel kuh tew port) — *Which dress? The one you're wearing.*
> **Watch out**
> - ✗ *Je prends celui.* → ✓ **Je prends celui-ci.** (zhuh prahN suh-lwee-see) — celui needs -ci, -là, qui, que or de after it.
> - "Paul's" is celui de Paul (suh-lwee duh pohl): French has no 's.
### C'est or il est?
*When:* c'est + a noun with its article or a name (C'est un ami, C'est Marie). il est / elle est + an adjective or a job on its own (Il est grand, Elle est médecin).
| French | Pronunciation | English | Followed by |
|---|---|---|---|
| c'est | seh | it is, this is, he is, she is | article + noun, a name, a stressed pronoun |
| ce sont | suh sohN | they are, these are | plural noun |
| il est | eel eh | he is, it is | adjective or job, no article |
| elle est | el eh | she is, it is | adjective or job, no article |
- **C'est un bon restaurant.** (seh tuhN bohN res-toh-rahN) — *It's a good restaurant.*
- **Il est médecin.** (eel eh mayd-saN) — *He's a doctor.*
- **C'est un médecin célèbre.** (seh tuhN mayd-saN say-lebr) — *He's a famous doctor.*
- **C'est beau !** (seh boh) — *That's beautiful! (about an idea or a view in general)*
> **Watch out**
> - ✗ *Il est un ami.* → ✓ **C'est un ami.** (seh tuhN nah-mee) — un/une + noun after "he is" → c'est.
> - ✗ *C'est médecin.* → ✓ **Il est médecin.** (eel eh mayd-saN) — a job with no article → il est / elle est.
## 5. Questions
A quick reference. For the full lessons with exercises, see the Asking questions topic.

See also: Asking questions (topic) · Where, when, how, why (lesson 3) · Who and what (lesson 4) · Which: quel (lesson 5).
### Question words
*When:* To ask for information. Put est-ce que after the word for the standard style: Où est-ce que tu vas ?
| French | Pronunciation | English | Example |
|---|---|---|---|
| qui | kee | who | Qui vient ce soir ? |
| que | kuh | what (formal, + inversion) | Que fais-tu ? |
| qu'est-ce que | kes-kuh | what (standard) | Qu'est-ce que tu fais ? |
| quoi | kwah | what (casual, at the end or after a preposition) | Tu fais quoi ? |
| où | oo | where | Où est-ce que tu habites ? |
| quand | kahN | when | Tu pars quand ? |
| comment | koh-mahN | how | Comment vas-tu ? |
| combien | kohN-byaN | how much, how many | C'est combien ? |
| combien de | kohN-byaN duh | how many (+ noun) | Combien de frères as-tu ? |
| pourquoi | poor-kwah | why | Pourquoi tu pars ? |
| parce que | pars-kuh | because | Parce qu'il pleut. |
- **Où est-ce que tu habites ?** (oo es-kuh tew ah-beet) — *Where do you live?*
- **Quand est-ce que tu pars ?** (kahN-tes-kuh tew par) — *When are you leaving?*
- **Qu'est-ce que c'est ?** (kes-kuh seh) — *What is it?*
- **Pourquoi est-ce que tu apprends le français ?** (poor-kwah es-kuh tew ah-prahN luh frahN-seh) — *Why are you learning French?*
> **Watch out**
> - ✗ *Quoi tu fais ?* → ✓ **Qu'est-ce que tu fais ?** (kes-kuh tew feh) — quoi goes at the end or after a preposition.
> - ✗ *Combien des frères as-tu ?* → ✓ **Combien de frères as-tu ?** (kohN-byaN duh frair ah-tew) — combien de + noun, no article.

See also: Asking questions, lesson 3 · Asking questions, lesson 4.
### Quel, quelle, quels, quelles: which, what
*When:* "Which" or "what" with a noun, or with être + noun. It agrees with the noun.
| French | Pronunciation | English | Gender / number |
|---|---|---|---|
| quel | kel | which, what | m. sing. |
| quelle | kel | which, what | f. sing. |
| quels | kel | which, what | m. pl.; kel z before a vowel |
| quelles | kel | which, what | f. pl.; kel z before a vowel |
- **Quelle heure est-il ?** (kel uhr eh-teel) — *What time is it?*
- **Quel âge as-tu ?** (kel ahzh ah-tew) — *How old are you?*
- **Quels amis viennent ?** (kel zah-mee vyen) — *Which friends are coming?*
- **Quel est ton nom ?** (kel eh tohN nohN) — *What is your name?*
> **Watch out**
> - ✗ *Quelle est ton nom ?* → ✓ **Quel est ton nom ?** (kel eh tohN nohN) — nom is masculine.
> - ✗ *Quel est-ce que tu veux ?* → ✓ **Qu'est-ce que tu veux ?** (kes-kuh tew vuh) — quel needs a noun or être.

See also: Asking questions, lesson 5.
### Lequel, laquelle: which one (Preview)
*When:* "Which one(s)?" when the noun is already clear. It agrees with that noun.
| French | Pronunciation | English | Gender / number |
|---|---|---|---|
| lequel | luh-kel | which one | m. sing. |
| laquelle | lah-kel | which one | f. sing. |
| lesquels | lay-kel | which ones | m. pl. |
| lesquelles | lay-kel | which ones | f. pl. |
- **Lequel préfères-tu ?** (luh-kel pray-fair-tew) — *Which one do you prefer? (a film)*
- **Laquelle veux-tu ?** (lah-kel vuh-tew) — *Which one do you want? (une tarte)*
- **Lesquels sont à toi ?** (lay-kel sohN tah twah) — *Which ones are yours? (des livres)*
> **Watch out**
> - ✗ *Quel préfères-tu ? (with no noun)* → ✓ **Lequel préfères-tu ?** (luh-kel pray-fair-tew) — no noun after it: use lequel.

See also: Asking questions, lesson 5.
## 6. Negation
### Negative words
*When:* ne goes before the verb and the second word after it; ne becomes n' before a vowel. In casual speech the ne is often dropped.
| French | Pronunciation | English | Example |
|---|---|---|---|
| ne ... pas | nuh ... pah | not | Je ne parle pas espagnol. |
| ne ... jamais | nuh ... zhah-meh | never | Il ne mange jamais de viande. |
| ne ... plus | nuh ... plew | no longer, not any more | Je n'habite plus ici. |
| ne ... rien | nuh ... ryaN | nothing, not anything | Je ne vois rien. |
| ne ... personne | nuh ... pair-sun | nobody, not anyone | Je ne connais personne. |
| ne ... que | nuh ... kuh | only | Je n'ai que dix euros. |
| ne ... ni ... ni | nuh ... nee ... nee | neither ... nor | Je ne bois ni thé ni café. |
- **Je n'ai jamais vu Paris.** (zhuh nay zhah-meh vew pah-ree) — *I've never seen Paris.*
- **Il n'y a personne.** (eel nee ah pair-sun) — *There's nobody there.*
- **Rien ne va.** (ryaN nuh vah) — *Nothing is going right. (rien as the subject comes first)*
- **Je ne bois que de l'eau.** (zhuh nuh bwah kuh duh loh) — *I only drink water.*
> **Watch out**
> - ✗ *Je ne vois pas rien.* → ✓ **Je ne vois rien.** (zhuh nuh vwah ryaN) — one negative word with ne, not pas + rien.
> - ne ... que is not really negative, so the article stays: Je n'ai que des pommes (zhuh nay kuh day pum).

See also: Pas de: after a negative.
### Where the negative goes
*When:* In compound tenses and with pronouns, ne ... pas wraps around the first verb and the pronouns in front of it.
| French | Pronunciation | English | Rule |
|---|---|---|---|
| Je ne parle pas. | zhuh nuh parl pah | I don't speak. | ne + verb + pas |
| Je n'ai pas mangé. | zhuh nay pah mahN-zhay | I didn't eat. | ne + avoir/être + pas + participle |
| Je ne suis pas allé. | zhuh nuh swee pah zah-lay | I didn't go. | same with être |
| Je ne le vois pas. | zhuh nuh luh vwah pah | I don't see him. | ne + pronoun + verb + pas |
| Je ne me lève pas. | zhuh nuh muh lev pah | I don't get up. | ne + reflexive pronoun + verb + pas |
| Je ne veux pas partir. | zhuh nuh vuh pah par-teer | I don't want to leave. | ne ... pas around the first verb |
| Je n'ai vu personne. | zhuh nay vew pair-sun | I didn't see anyone. | personne goes after the participle |
- **Elle n'est pas encore arrivée.** (el neh pah zahN-kor ah-ree-vay) — *She hasn't arrived yet.*
- **Je ne l'ai jamais vu.** (zhuh nuh lay zhah-meh vew) — *I've never seen it.*
- **Ne pas toucher.** (nuh pah too-shay) — *Do not touch. (before an infinitive both words go together)*
> **Watch out**
> - ✗ *Je n'ai mangé pas.* → ✓ **Je n'ai pas mangé.** (zhuh nay pah mahN-zhay) — pas goes right after avoir / être.
> - ✗ *Je ne vois le pas.* → ✓ **Je ne le vois pas.** (zhuh nuh luh vwah pah) — the pronoun stays glued to the verb.

See also: Reflexive verbs, lesson 3 (negatives).
## 7. Adjectives
### Regular agreement patterns
*When:* Adjectives agree with the noun: add -e for feminine, -s for plural, -es for feminine plural. Some endings change.
| French | Pronunciation | English | Pattern (m. → f.) |
|---|---|---|---|
| grand, grande | grahN, grahNd | tall, big | + e |
| petit, petite | puh-tee, puh-teet | small | + e (the t is now said) |
| jeune | zhuhn | young | ends in e: no change |
| grands, grandes | grahN, grahNd | tall, big | pl. + s / + es |
| heureux, heureuse | uh-ruh, uh-ruhz | happy | -eux → -euse |
| sportif, sportive | spor-teef, spor-teev | sporty | -if → -ive |
| cher, chère | shair, shair | expensive, dear | -er → -ère |
| premier, première | pruh-myay, pruh-myair | first | -ier → -ière |
| naturel, naturelle | nah-tew-rel, nah-tew-rel | natural | -el → -elle |
| bon, bonne | bohN, bun | good | -on → -onne |
| italien, italienne | ee-tah-lyaN, ee-tah-lyen | Italian | -ien → -ienne |
- **Ma sœur est grande.** (mah suhr eh grahNd) — *My sister is tall.*
- **Elles sont heureuses.** (el sohN tuh-ruhz) — *They are happy.*
- **C'est une bonne idée.** (seh tewn bun ee-day) — *It's a good idea.*
- **Les chaussures sont chères.** (lay shoh-sewr sohN shair) — *The shoes are expensive.*
> **Watch out**
> - ✗ *une maison petit* → ✓ **une petite maison** (ewn puh-teet meh-zohN) — agree, and petit goes before the noun (BAGS).
> - Adding -e often makes a silent final consonant heard: petit (puh-tee) → petite (puh-teet).
### Common irregular adjectives
*When:* These change more. beau, nouveau and vieux have a special masculine form before a vowel or mute h. Plurals: beaux, belles · nouveaux, nouvelles · vieux, vieilles.
| French | Pronunciation | English | Forms |
|---|---|---|---|
| beau | boh | beautiful, handsome | m. |
| bel | bel | beautiful, handsome | m. before a vowel: un bel homme |
| belle | bel | beautiful | f. |
| nouveau | noo-voh | new | m. |
| nouvel | noo-vel | new | m. before a vowel: un nouvel ami |
| nouvelle | noo-vel | new | f. |
| vieux | vyuh | old | m. (pl. vieux) |
| vieil | vyehy | old | m. before a vowel: un vieil homme |
| vieille | vyehy | old | f. |
| blanc | blahN | white | m. |
| blanche | blahNsh | white | f. |
| long | lohN | long | m. |
| longue | lohNg | long | f. |
| gentil | zhahN-tee | kind, nice | m. |
| gentille | zhahN-teey | kind, nice | f. |
- **C'est un bel appartement.** (seh tuhN bel ah-par-tuh-mahN) — *It's a beautiful flat.*
- **J'ai un nouvel ordinateur.** (zhay uhN noo-vel or-dee-nah-tuhr) — *I have a new computer.*
- **Ma grand-mère est une vieille dame.** (mah grahN-mair eh tewn vyehy dahm) — *My grandmother is an old lady.*
- **Elle porte une robe blanche.** (el port ewn rob blahNsh) — *She's wearing a white dress.*
> **Watch out**
> - ✗ *un beau homme* → ✓ **un bel homme** (uhN bel um) — bel, nouvel, vieil before a vowel or mute h (singular only).
> - ✗ *une robe blance* → ✓ **une robe blanche** (ewn rob blahNsh)
### Adjectives that go before the noun: BAGS
*When:* Most adjectives go after the noun (une voiture rouge). A short list of common ones goes before: Beauty, Age, Goodness, Size.
| French | Pronunciation | English | BAGS |
|---|---|---|---|
| beau, joli | boh, zhoh-lee | beautiful, pretty | Beauty |
| jeune, vieux, nouveau | zhuhn, vyuh, noo-voh | young, old, new | Age |
| bon, mauvais | bohN, moh-veh | good, bad | Goodness |
| grand, petit, gros | grahN, puh-tee, groh | big or tall, small, fat or big | Size |
| une jolie maison | ewn zhoh-lee meh-zohN | a pretty house | before |
| une voiture rouge | ewn vwah-tewr roozh | a red car | after (colour) |
| un film intéressant | uhN feelm aN-tay-reh-sahN | an interesting film | after (most adjectives) |
- **C'est un petit village.** (seh tuhN puh-tee vee-lahzh) — *It's a small village.*
- **J'ai un bon ami.** (zhay uhN bohN nah-mee) — *I have a good friend.*
- **Il a une voiture noire.** (eel ah ewn vwah-tewr nwahr) — *He has a black car.*
> **Watch out**
> - ✗ *une rouge voiture* → ✓ **une voiture rouge** (ewn vwah-tewr roozh) — colours and nationalities go after.
> - Before an adjective in the plural, des usually becomes de: de bons amis (duh bohN zah-mee). This is a B1 detail; casual speech often keeps des.
## 8. Prepositions
### Prepositions of place
*When:* To say where something is. Remember à + le = au and de + le = du: à côté du lit, près de la gare.
| French | Pronunciation | English | With le, la, les |
|---|---|---|---|
| sur | sewr | on |  |
| sous | soo | under |  |
| devant | duh-vahN | in front of |  |
| derrière | dair-yair | behind |  |
| dans | dahN | in, inside |  |
| entre | ahN-truh | between |  |
| à côté de | ah koh-tay duh | next to | du / de la / des |
| près de | preh duh | near | du / de la / des |
| loin de | lwaN duh | far from | du / de la / des |
| en face de | ahN fahs duh | opposite | du / de la / des |
- **Le chat est sous la table.** (luh shah eh soo lah tah-bluh) — *The cat is under the table.*
- **La banque est à côté de la poste.** (lah bahNk eh tah koh-tay duh lah post) — *The bank is next to the post office.*
- **J'habite près du parc.** (zhah-beet preh dew park) — *I live near the park.*
- **Le café est en face de l'hôtel.** (luh kah-fay eh tahN fahs duh loh-tel) — *The café is opposite the hotel.*
> **Watch out**
> - ✗ *près de le parc* → ✓ **près du parc** (preh dew park) — de + le = du.
> - ✗ *à côté la gare* → ✓ **à côté de la gare** (ah koh-tay duh lah gar) — keep the de.

See also: à and de + the article.
### Cities and countries: à, en, au, aux
*When:* "In" or "to" a place. Most countries ending in -e are feminine (la France); a few are not (le Mexique, le Cambodge).
| French | Pronunciation | English | Use with |
|---|---|---|---|
| à Paris | ah pah-ree | in / to Paris | à + city |
| en France | ahN frahNs | in / to France | en + f. country |
| en Italie | ahN nee-tah-lee | in / to Italy | en + country starting with a vowel |
| au Canada | oh kah-nah-dah | in / to Canada | au + m. country |
| au Japon | oh zhah-pohN | in / to Japan | au + m. country |
| aux États-Unis | oh zay-tah-zew-nee | in / to the United States | aux + pl. country |
| de France | duh frahNs | from France | de + f. country |
| du Canada | dew kah-nah-dah | from Canada | du + m. country |
- **J'habite à Londres.** (zhah-beet ah lohN-druh) — *I live in London.*
- **Nous allons en Espagne.** (noo zah-lohN ahN nes-pahny) — *We're going to Spain.*
- **Il travaille au Portugal.** (eel trah-vahy oh por-tew-gahl) — *He works in Portugal.*
- **Elle revient des États-Unis.** (el ruh-vyaN day zay-tah-zew-nee) — *She's coming back from the United States.*
> **Watch out**
> - ✗ *à France* → ✓ **en France** (ahN frahNs) — à is for cities; countries take en / au / aux.
> - ✗ *en Canada* → ✓ **au Canada** (oh kah-nah-dah) — masculine countries take au.
## 9. Verb reference
A summary only. The full verb tables, with every form and a Listen button, are in Learn.

See also: Learn: all verbs · Lesson 2: regular -er verbs · parler · finir · attendre · aller · venir · se lever · Reflexive verbs, lesson 4 (past and future).
### Present-tense endings
*When:* Regular verbs: drop -er, -ir or -re and add the endings. -er: -e, -es, -e, -ons, -ez, -ent · -ir: -is, -is, -it, -issons, -issez, -issent · -re: -s, -s, (nothing), -ons, -ez, -ent.
| Person | -er: parler | -ir: finir | -re: attendre |
|---|---|---|---|
| je | je parle (zhuh parl) | je finis (zhuh fee-nee) | j'attends (zhah-tahN) |
| tu | tu parles (tew parl) | tu finis (tew fee-nee) | tu attends (tew ah-tahN) |
| il/elle | il parle (eel parl) | il finit (eel fee-nee) | il attend (eel ah-tahN) |
| nous | nous parlons (noo par-lohN) | nous finissons (noo fee-nee-sohN) | nous attendons (noo zah-tahN-dohN) |
| vous | vous parlez (voo par-lay) | vous finissez (voo fee-nee-say) | vous attendez (voo zah-tahN-day) |
| ils/elles | ils parlent (eel parl) | ils finissent (eel fee-nees) | ils attendent (eel zah-tahNd) |
- **Nous finissons à cinq heures.** (noo fee-nee-sohN ah saN kuhr) — *We finish at five.*
- **Il attend le bus.** (eel ah-tahN luh bews) — *He's waiting for the bus.*
> **Watch out**
> - The je, tu, il and ils forms of -er verbs all sound the same: parle, parles, parle, parlent = parl.
> - -ir verbs like partir, sortir and dormir do NOT follow finir: je pars, nous partons.

See also: parler · finir · attendre · partir.
### Verbs that take être in the passé composé
*When:* These verbs (mostly movement or change of state) and ALL pronominal verbs form the passé composé with être, and the participle agrees with the subject. Memory aid: DR & MRS VANDERTRAMPP.
| French | Pronunciation | English | Past (je) |
|---|---|---|---|
| devenir | duh-vuh-neer | to become | je suis devenu(e) |
| revenir | ruh-vuh-neer | to come back | je suis revenu(e) |
| monter | mohN-tay | to go up | je suis monté(e) |
| rester | res-tay | to stay | je suis resté(e) |
| sortir | sor-teer | to go out | je suis sorti(e) |
| venir | vuh-neer | to come | je suis venu(e) |
| aller | ah-lay | to go | je suis allé(e) |
| naître | neh-truh | to be born | je suis né(e) |
| descendre | deh-sahN-druh | to go down | je suis descendu(e) |
| entrer | ahN-tray | to enter | je suis entré(e) |
| rentrer | rahN-tray | to go home | je suis rentré(e) |
| tomber | tohN-bay | to fall | je suis tombé(e) |
| retourner | ruh-toor-nay | to return | je suis retourné(e) |
| arriver | ah-ree-vay | to arrive | je suis arrivé(e) |
| mourir | moo-reer | to die | je suis mort(e) |
| partir | par-teer | to leave | je suis parti(e) |
| passer | pah-say | to pass by | je suis passé(e) |
| se lever (and all reflexive verbs) | suh luh-vay | to get up | je me suis levé(e) |
- **Elle est arrivée hier.** (el eh tah-ree-vay yair) — *She arrived yesterday.*
- **Nous sommes allés au cinéma.** (noo sum zah-lay oh see-nay-mah) — *We went to the cinema.*
- **Je me suis levé à sept heures.** (zhuh muh swee luh-vay ah set uhr) — *I got up at seven.*
> **Watch out**
> - ✗ *J'ai allé* → ✓ **Je suis allé(e)** (zhuh swee zah-lay)
> - With a direct object, monter, descendre, sortir, rentrer and passer take avoir: J'ai monté les valises (zhay mohN-tay lay vah-leez).

See also: Reflexive verbs, lesson 4 (past).
### Futur simple: endings and irregular stems
*When:* "Will". Regular verbs: the infinitive (drop the final e of -re) + -ai, -as, -a, -ons, -ez, -ont. Irregular verbs use a special stem with the same endings.
| French | Pronunciation | English | Ending / stem |
|---|---|---|---|
| je parlerai | zhuh par-luh-ray | I will speak | -ai |
| tu parleras | tew par-luh-rah | you will speak | -as |
| il parlera | eel par-luh-rah | he will speak | -a |
| nous parlerons | noo par-luh-rohN | we will speak | -ons |
| vous parlerez | voo par-luh-ray | you will speak | -ez |
| ils parleront | eel par-luh-rohN | they will speak | -ont |
| je serai | zhuh suh-ray | I will be | être: ser- |
| j'aurai | zhoh-ray | I will have | avoir: aur- |
| j'irai | zhee-ray | I will go | aller: ir- |
| je ferai | zhuh fuh-ray | I will do | faire: fer- |
| je pourrai | zhuh poo-ray | I will be able to | pouvoir: pourr- |
| je voudrai | zhuh voo-dray | I will want | vouloir: voudr- |
| je devrai | zhuh duh-vray | I will have to | devoir: devr- |
| je saurai | zhuh soh-ray | I will know | savoir: saur- |
| je verrai | zhuh veh-ray | I will see | voir: verr- |
| je viendrai | zhuh vyaN-dray | I will come | venir: viendr- |
| je tiendrai | zhuh tyaN-dray | I will hold | tenir: tiendr- |
| je recevrai | zhuh ruh-suh-vray | I will receive | recevoir: recevr- |
| j'enverrai | zhahN-veh-ray | I will send | envoyer: enverr- |
| je courrai | zhuh koor-ray | I will run | courir: courr- |
| je mourrai | zhuh moor-ray | I will die | mourir: mourr- |
| il faudra | eel foh-drah | it will be necessary | falloir: faudr- |
| il pleuvra | eel pluh-vrah | it will rain | pleuvoir: pleuvr- |
- **Demain, il fera beau.** (duh-maN, eel fuh-rah boh) — *Tomorrow the weather will be nice.*
- **Nous irons en France.** (noo zee-rohN ahN frahNs) — *We will go to France.*
> **Watch out**
> - The endings are the present of avoir (ai, as, a, ons, ez, ont); the stem always ends in r.
> - ✗ *je allerai* → ✓ **j'irai** (zhee-ray)
> - The near future is more common in speech: aller + infinitive, Je vais partir (zhuh veh par-teer).

See also: Reflexive verbs, lesson 4 (future).
## 10. Everyday basics
### Numbers 0–20
*When:* Counting, prices, ages and phone numbers. Learn 0–16 by heart; 17, 18 and 19 are 10 + 7, 8, 9.
| French | Pronunciation | English |
|---|---|---|
| zéro | zay-roh | 0 |
| un | uhN | 1 (une with a f. noun: ewn) |
| deux | duh | 2 |
| trois | trwah | 3 |
| quatre | kah-truh | 4 |
| cinq | saNk | 5 |
| six | sees | 6 |
| sept | set | 7 |
| huit | weet | 8 |
| neuf | nuhf | 9 |
| dix | dees | 10 |
| onze | ohNz | 11 |
| douze | dooz | 12 |
| treize | trez | 13 |
| quatorze | kah-torz | 14 |
| quinze | kaNz | 15 |
| seize | sez | 16 |
| dix-sept | dee-set | 17 |
| dix-huit | deez-weet | 18 |
| dix-neuf | deez-nuhf | 19 |
| vingt | vaN | 20 |
- **J'ai trois enfants.** (zhay trwah zahN-fahN) — *I have three children.*
- **Il a dix-huit ans.** (eel ah deez-wee tahN) — *He is eighteen.*
> **Watch out**
> - Before a consonant, cinq, six, huit and dix often lose their final sound: six livres (see leevr). Before a vowel they link: six ans (see zahN).
> - ✗ *Il est dix-huit.* → ✓ **Il a dix-huit ans.** (eel ah deez-wee tahN) — age uses avoir and always ans.
### Numbers 21–100
*When:* From 70, French counts in twenties: 70 = 60 + 10, 80 = 4 × 20, 90 = 4 × 20 + 10. Use et un for 21, 31, 41, 51 and 61, and et onze for 71; there is no et in 81 or 91.
| French | Pronunciation | English | Built as |
|---|---|---|---|
| vingt et un | vaN-tay-uhN | 21 | 20 et 1 |
| vingt-deux | vaNt-duh | 22 | 20-2 |
| trente | trahNt | 30 |  |
| trente et un | trahN-tay-uhN | 31 | 30 et 1 |
| quarante | kah-rahNt | 40 |  |
| cinquante | saN-kahNt | 50 |  |
| soixante | swah-sahNt | 60 |  |
| soixante-dix | swah-sahNt-dees | 70 | 60 + 10 |
| soixante et onze | swah-sahN-tay-ohNz | 71 | 60 et 11 |
| soixante-douze | swah-sahNt-dooz | 72 | 60 + 12 |
| quatre-vingts | kah-truh-vaN | 80 | 4 × 20 (with s) |
| quatre-vingt-un | kah-truh-vaN-uhN | 81 | 4 × 20 + 1 (no s, no et) |
| quatre-vingt-dix | kah-truh-vaN-dees | 90 | 4 × 20 + 10 |
| quatre-vingt-onze | kah-truh-vaN-ohNz | 91 | 4 × 20 + 11 |
| quatre-vingt-dix-neuf | kah-truh-vaN-deez-nuhf | 99 | 4 × 20 + 19 |
| cent | sahN | 100 |  |
- **Ma grand-mère a quatre-vingts ans.** (mah grahN-mair ah kah-truh-vaN zahN) — *My grandmother is eighty.*
- **Ça coûte soixante-quinze euros.** (sah koot swah-sahNt-kaNz uh-roh) — *It costs seventy-five euros.*
- **Il y a trente et un jours en mai.** (eel ee ah trahN-tay-uhN zhoor ahN meh) — *There are thirty-one days in May.*
> **Watch out**
> - ✗ *quatre-vingts-un* → ✓ **quatre-vingt-un** (kah-truh-vaN-uhN) — quatre-vingts keeps its s only when nothing follows.
> - ✗ *quatre-vingt et un* → ✓ **quatre-vingt-un** (kah-truh-vaN-uhN) — no et in 81 or 91.
> - In Belgium and Switzerland you'll also hear septante (70) and nonante (90); in Switzerland huitante (80).
### Ordinal numbers: first, second...
*When:* Add -ième to the number (drop a final e). Dates use le premier, then plain numbers: le deux mai.
| French | Pronunciation | English | Note |
|---|---|---|---|
| premier | pruh-myay | first | m.; 1er |
| première | pruh-myair | first | f.; 1re |
| deuxième | duh-zyem | second | 2e |
| troisième | trwah-zyem | third | 3e |
| quatrième | kah-tree-yem | fourth | drop the e |
| cinquième | saN-kyem | fifth | add u |
| neuvième | nuh-vyem | ninth | f → v |
| dixième | dee-zyem | tenth |  |
| vingtième | vaN-tyem | twentieth |  |
- **J'habite au troisième étage.** (zhah-beet oh trwah-zyem ay-tahzh) — *I live on the third floor.*
- **C'est le premier mai.** (seh luh pruh-myay meh) — *It's the first of May.*
- **C'est le deux mai.** (seh luh duh meh) — *It's the second of May.*
> **Watch out**
> - ✗ *le deuxième mai* → ✓ **le deux mai** (luh duh meh) — only the 1st takes premier in dates.
### Days of the week
*When:* No capital letters in French. Use le for a regular day: le lundi = on Mondays. For one day, no word for "on": lundi = on Monday.
| French | Pronunciation | English |
|---|---|---|
| lundi | luhN-dee | Monday |
| mardi | mar-dee | Tuesday |
| mercredi | mair-kruh-dee | Wednesday |
| jeudi | zhuh-dee | Thursday |
| vendredi | vahN-druh-dee | Friday |
| samedi | sahm-dee | Saturday |
| dimanche | dee-mahNsh | Sunday |
- **Je travaille le lundi.** (zhuh trah-vahy luh luhN-dee) — *I work on Mondays.*
- **On se voit samedi ?** (ohN suh vwah sahm-dee) — *Shall we meet on Saturday?*
> **Watch out**
> - ✗ *Lundi* → ✓ **lundi** (luhN-dee) — no capital letter.
> - ✗ *sur lundi* → ✓ **lundi** (luhN-dee) — no word for "on" with a single day.
### Months
*When:* No capital letters. In a month: en mai or au mois de mai.
| French | Pronunciation | English |
|---|---|---|
| janvier | zhahN-vyay | January |
| février | fay-vree-yay | February |
| mars | mars | March |
| avril | ah-vreel | April |
| mai | meh | May |
| juin | zhwaN | June |
| juillet | zhwee-yeh | July |
| août | oot | August |
| septembre | sep-tahN-bruh | September |
| octobre | ok-toh-bruh | October |
| novembre | noh-vahN-bruh | November |
| décembre | day-sahN-bruh | December |
- **Mon anniversaire est en juillet.** (mohN nah-nee-vair-sair eh tahN zhwee-yeh) — *My birthday is in July.*
- **Je pars en août.** (zhuh par ahN noot) — *I'm leaving in August.*
- **Il fait froid en décembre.** (eel feh frwah ahN day-sahN-bruh) — *It's cold in December.*
> **Watch out**
> - ✗ *Juillet* → ✓ **juillet** (zhwee-yeh) — no capital letter.
> - ✗ *dans mai* → ✓ **en mai** (ahN meh) — use en (or au mois de) with a month.
### Telling the time
*When:* Il est + number + heure(s). Schedules, trains and shops use the 24-hour clock.
| French | Pronunciation | English | Time |
|---|---|---|---|
| Quelle heure est-il ? | kel uhr eh-teel | What time is it? |  |
| Il est une heure. | eel eh tewn uhr | It's one o'clock. | 1:00 |
| Il est deux heures. | eel eh duh zuhr | It's two o'clock. | 2:00 |
| Il est trois heures cinq. | eel eh trwah zuhr saNk | It's five past three. | 3:05 |
| Il est quatre heures et quart. | eel eh kah-truhr ay kar | It's quarter past four. | 4:15 |
| Il est cinq heures et demie. | eel eh saN kuhr ay duh-mee | It's half past five. | 5:30 |
| Il est six heures moins le quart. | eel eh see zuhr mwaN luh kar | It's quarter to six. | 5:45 |
| Il est sept heures moins dix. | eel eh set uhr mwaN dees | It's ten to seven. | 6:50 |
| Il est midi. | eel eh mee-dee | It's noon. | 12:00 |
| Il est minuit. | eel eh mee-nwee | It's midnight. | 0:00 |
| Il est dix-huit heures trente. | eel eh deez-wee tuhr trahNt | It's 6:30 pm. | 18:30 (24-hour) |
| à huit heures | ah wee tuhr | at eight o'clock | at |
- **Le film commence à vingt heures.** (luh feelm koh-mahNs ah vaN tuhr) — *The film starts at 8 pm.*
- **On se retrouve à midi et demi ?** (ohN suh ruh-troov ah mee-dee ay duh-mee) — *Shall we meet at half past twelve?*
> **Watch out**
> - ✗ *Il est deux.* → ✓ **Il est deux heures.** (eel eh duh zuhr) — always say heure(s).
> - et demie after heure(s) (f.), but midi et demi and minuit et demi (no e).

See also: Asking questions, lesson 5 (Quelle heure est-il ?).
### Common time expressions
*When:* Words for when and how often. They usually go at the start or the end of the sentence.
| French | Pronunciation | English |
|---|---|---|
| aujourd'hui | oh-zhoor-dwee | today |
| demain | duh-maN | tomorrow |
| hier | yair | yesterday |
| maintenant | maNt-nahN | now |
| ce matin | suh mah-taN | this morning |
| ce soir | suh swahr | this evening, tonight |
| cette semaine | set suh-men | this week |
| le week-end | luh wee-kend | at the weekend |
| la semaine prochaine | lah suh-men proh-shen | next week |
| l'année dernière | lah-nay dair-nyair | last year |
| tous les jours | too lay zhoor | every day |
| souvent | soo-vahN | often |
| toujours | too-zhoor | always, still |
| parfois | par-fwah | sometimes |
| il y a deux jours | eel ee ah duh zhoor | two days ago |
| depuis | duh-pwee | since, for |
- **J'apprends le français depuis un an.** (zhah-prahN luh frahN-seh duh-pwee uhN nahN) — *I've been learning French for a year.*
- **Je suis arrivé il y a deux jours.** (zhuh swee zah-ree-vay eel ee ah duh zhoor) — *I arrived two days ago.*
> **Watch out**
> - ✗ *J'apprends le français pour un an.* → ✓ **J'apprends le français depuis un an.** (zhah-prahN luh frahN-seh duh-pwee uhN nahN) — depuis + present for something still going on.
